mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to tightened near-term discounting of corporate cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns remain positive whenever the trigger occurs, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS spikes and negative 20d returns is statistically insignificant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > INDPRO for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market weakening detected by dual indicator divergence
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive whenever the trigger occurs, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a Granger causality test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 5% year-over-year growth predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects resilient consumer demand and upward earnings revisions.
failure_condition: Over 30 consecutive months of positive HOUST YoY growth, 20-day forward returns never exceed the mean of the prior 12 months (median test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 0.5% for three months) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it indicates weakening aggregate supply capacity.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive during all such contractions, or the effect is not robust across multiple backtests (out-of-sample p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% and coincides with a 2% monthly rise in FEDFUNDS, the S&P 500 expects a positive 20-day forward return as investors anticipate a pause in rate hikes.
failure_condition: The interaction is not predictive in walk-forward tests (p > 0.05) or the 20-day forward return is negative whenever the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies) would be expected to be proxied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% in a month with rising payrolls (PAYEMS > 200K), predicting a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market tightness increases.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening detected by dual indicators
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is never positive during such triggers, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL < 3% for two consecutive months) in a tightening cycle is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it reduces expectations of future rate hikes.
regime_hint: Low-inflation environment during rate hike cycle
failure_condition: Over 12 months of CPIAUCSL < 3%, the 20-day forward return is never positive, or the effect is not significant in a rolling Granger causality test.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline exceeding 2% in a month when the unemployment rate is above 6% signals supply-side weakness in a slack economy, predicting a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive during all such events, or the interaction effect is not robust (p > 0.05) in a cross-validation setting.
